reader.requirement: At --std 85 the FILE STATUS operand must resolve to a data item of category alphanumeric exactly two character positions long, and must be refused if defined in the File Section (FD or SD record), the Report Section or the Communication Section; Working-Storage and Linkage items (and a level-66 rename of such an item) are legal.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.SubscriptedClauseOperands (true only at 2002) gates the OCCURS arm; Edition.DialectLevel < 2002 picks the 1985 wording and citation for the OCCURS and shape messages
Edition.SubscriptedClauseOperands: only 2002 screens written subscripts; 85 reaches the item unchanged as 2023 does
below 2002 a sum counter is the operand (SumCounterOperand85, §1985:XIII.3.9.3 SR10d) and the clause's own rules then judge it; other report entries refused as at 2023

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|SubscriptedClauseOperands|ConstructRegistry over FileControlBinder.Resolve.cs, DataBinder.ResolveClauseOperand, ItemCategory.cs; the shape predicate FileStatusShapeFault has no edition switch (its LocalStorage admission is unreachable at 85: LOCAL-STORAGE is refused COBOL0900).
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: only the diagnostic wording/citation differs (1985 vs 2023 SR2 text), the OCCURS arm cites §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR4 below 2002, and at 85 a sum counter resolves as the operand (then refused for category numeric); the accept/refuse set for this rule is the same as at 2023.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: witnesses cover numeric (g85_y94), File Section record (pb5627), edited and OCCURS (pb5627 siblings), level 66 (pb5801); not exercised: wrong length (PIC X, X(3)), alphabetic, Communication Section, Report Section, SD record, Linkage legal side, group of two positions.

reader.notes: Every conjunct (category, size, three barred sections) is screened post-build by ScreenFileStatusItem/FileStatusShapeFault with 1985 wording. A two-position group (even of PIC 9 subordinates, fs11) is accepted as alphanumeric: §1985:IV.4.3.3 makes a group's class alphanumeric while its table lists every category for a group, so the 1985 text is not explicit; the reading matches GnuCOBOL and the 2023 rule. The Report Section half is enforced by the report-reference refusal or, for a 1985 sum counter, by the category refusal.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 (run_probe.py, runs under refute-1985-228/runs): fs66fd (66 RFS RENAMES an FD record field) COBOL2455 'defined in the file section'; fsxb (PIC XB) COBOL2455 category-alphanumeric-edited; fsjust (PIC AA) COBOL2455 category-alphabetic; fsnn (PIC NN) COBOL2455 category-national plus COBOL0900 national requires 2002; fs66thru (66 R66 RENAMES A1 THRU A2, both PIC X) compiles and runs; fsnum9 (01 FSG with two PIC 9 subordinates) compiles and runs. Every elementary conjunct and every barred section is screened. The verdict on groups rests on a reading: cite.py --check "§1985:IV.4.3.3" "The class of a group item is treated at object time as alphanumeric" -> OK, but the same clause's table gives a Nonelementary (Group) item CLASS Alphanumeric with CATEGORY listed as Alphabetic, Numeric, Numeric edited, Alphanumeric edited or Alphanumeric, and the text never says which category a group takes. cite.py --check "§1985:VII.2.5.3 SR2" "two-character data item of the category alphanumeric" -> OK. Under the reading that a group whose subordinates are all numeric is of category numeric, fsnum9 must be refused and the compiler under-rejects; under the reader's reading (a group is alphanumeric) it conforms.
